summary: Markets closed higher Wednesday as Wall Street staged a partial recovery despite a complex backdrop of geopolitical tension and mixed corporate signals, with the overall mood cautiously optimistic but fragile. The dominant macro driver remains the escalating U.S.-Iran conflict, with American strikes targeting Iranian assets including airlines and digital infrastructure, while Iran has retaliated by blacklisting vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz and attacking a Saudi-flagged ship, killing two sailors — directly threatening a critical global oil chokepoint. On the corporate front, Broadcom shares fell 5% after weak forward guidance overshadowed a quarterly earnings beat, while Johnson & Johnson continued its march toward record highs on strong fundamental drivers, and investors rotated toward defensive stocks to hedge against outsized AI-sector exposure. The primary risk factors commanding investor attention are a potential full-scale Middle East war disrupting energy supplies, rising UK gilt yields hitting 19-year highs signaling global bond market stress, and the prospect that U.S.-Iran hostilities could intensify after November elections despite Trump's assertion the campaign will be brief. In the short term, markets will remain headline-driven and volatile, with energy prices, Hormuz shipping developments, and any diplomatic signals between Washington and Tehran serving as the key swing factors for sentiment.
